knowledge:
- key_parameters: gene.col=Character string specifying the column name for gene identifiers in the input data frame (e.g., "GeneName") ;; condition.col=Character string specifying the column name for conditions/pathogens in the input data frame (e.g., "condition") ;; simplify=Logical value; if TRUE (default), returns a matrix of estimated ccg effects and local FDRs; if FALSE, returns a list containing the matrix, the lmer model fit, and the estimated ag and bcg values ;; weight=Argument to incorporate RNAi weights into the linear mixed model fit based on siRNA quality or library information ;; ignore=Argument to specify the minimum number of required siRNA replicates for each gene ;; threshold=FDR threshold used in hitheatmap and sharedness to filter significant genes (e.g., 0.2 or 0.4) ;; sharedness.score=Logical value in hitheatmap; if TRUE, adds a row visualizing the sharedness score ;; na.omit=Argument in hitheatmap to omit incomplete combinations of genes and conditions from the plot
- alternatives: None mentioned; the package internally utilizes the lmer function from the lme4 package for linear mixed model estimation and Efron's empirical Bayes/local FDR estimation methods.
- when_to_use: Use this package when analyzing high-throughput RNAi screens (or similar knock-down assays) performed in parallel under multiple conditions (e.g., different pathogens, cell lines, or treatments) where each gene is targeted by multiple independent siRNAs (different seeds) per condition.
- pitfalls: Biological replicates (experimental results with identical siRNA seeds and identical conditions) must be averaged before fitting the model ;; The input data must contain several independent siRNA measurements per gene and condition to ensure statistical power ;; Missing combinations of genes and conditions will result in NA values in the output, which must be handled appropriately (e.g., using na.omit in plotting).

workflows.name: parallel_mixed_model_analysis
workflows.intent: Fit the Parallel Mixed Model to parallel RNAi screen data to estimate gene effects and local FDRs, calculate sharedness scores, and visualize the hits.
input: screen_data.csv (A data frame containing columns for gene identifiers, conditions, and RNAi readouts, with multiple independent siRNA measurements per gene/condition and averaged biological replicates)
workflows.stages: 1. Fit the Parallel Mixed Model using pmm ;; 2. Calculate the sharedness score using sharedness ;; 3. Visualize the results using hitheatmap
workflows.code:
library(pmm)
data(kinome)
head(kinome)
fit1 <- pmm(kinome, "InfectionIndex", gene.col = "GeneName",
condition.col = "condition")
head(fit1)
fit2 <- pmm(kinome, "InfectionIndex", gene.col = "GeneName",
condition.col = "condition", simplify = FALSE)
class(fit2)
names(fit2)
identical(fit1,fit2[[1]])
kinome$InfectionIndex[kinome$GeneName == "AAK1" &
    kinome$condition == "ADENO"] <- rep(NA,12)
fit3 <- pmm(kinome ,"InfectionIndex", gene.col = "GeneName")
head(fit3,3)
hitheatmap(fit1, threshold = 0.2)
hitheatmap(fit1, threshold = 0.4, cex.main = 2,
main = "My modified plot", col.main = "white",
col.axis = "white", cex.axis = 0.8, bg = "black", mar = c(6,8,4,6))
sh <- sharedness(fit1, threshold = 0.2)
sh[order(sh$Sharedness),]
hitheatmap(fit1, sharedness.score = TRUE, main = "My hits found by PMM")
